answer: Each identity anchors to one registered tide-gauge station at a named ocean lagoon: a $900 gauge bolted to a fixed pier, signing each epoch's tide curve with the epoch nonce, checked by a summit GNSS beacon. One station, one vote; two sharing a gauge collapse to one vote and burn a $50 stake, and no fresh signed curve means no vote. A farm wanting 100 votes must buy and keep 100 real gauges at 100 real lagoons, about $900 each plus $80 a year, each needing a season of logged tides, with no way to pre-raise gauges in parallel. Honest operators register once, then sign each epoch nearly free.
